verdict.reason: Smooth, continuous low-altitude aerial flight toward and over a rock butte gives strong parallax over a static, real, sharp canyon scene with no cuts or overlays.

Continuous low-altitude aerial flight toward and over a textured Grand Canyon butte, with the near rock growing against a nearly unchanged distant backdrop, so there is real parallax over a static real scene with no cuts, overlays or moving objects.
Smooth drone glide past a canyon spur gives real parallax between the near ridge and the distant butte over a static, sharp, real landscape with no cuts or overlays.

Smooth drone arc along a canyon rim, where the near ridge turns from end-on to side-on while the distant butte drifts the other way, so there is real parallax over a static, well-textured real scene (large scale makes metric depth harder).
Low-altitude flight along a river in a rocky canyon: the sandbar and slopes shift against the distant mesa (clear parallax), and the shot is continuous and sharp, with only the river surface moving.
Continuous low-altitude forward flight along a river in a canyon, with clear parallax from the nearby hillside and sandbars over a static real scene; only the river surface moves.
Low-altitude drone flight past a canyon cliff, with strong foreground-to-background parallax over a static, textured real scene and no cuts, overlays or moving objects.

A low-altitude drone-style flight past a canyon cliff shows clear foreground/background parallax over a static, sharp, real landscape with no cuts or overlays, though much of the frame is distant terrain.
